chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb, who said:

A man came to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said: 'I was a slave to a people, and I married a free woman without the permission of my master. Then they freed me after that. Should I renew my marriage to her at the time I was freed?' He said to him: 'Did they know about you when you married while you were their slave?' He said: 'Yes, and they remained silent regarding me and did not object.' He said: 'Then he said to him: Their silence after their knowledge is their consent. Maintain your first marriage.'
ai.seo_question: Does a slave's marriage to a free woman require renewal after manumission if the master knew and remained silent?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of *sukut* (silence) as *iqar* (acknowledgment) in marital contracts, ruling that a master's knowledge of a slave's marriage without objection implies consent. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic view that explicit permission is not always required if the owner's silence indicates acquiescence, thereby preserving the validity of the initial union upon manumission. It underscores the flexibility in *fiqh al-nikah* regarding the status of *sahib al-yamin* (slave) and the importance of contextual evidence in validating legal acts.
